chunks: The obligatory prayer: Dhuhr is four units, Asr is four units, Maghrib is three units, the last 'Isha is four units, and Fajr is two units. The total obligatory prayer is seventeen units, and the Sunnah is thirty-four units.

Among them, four units after Maghrib are not shortened on journey or in residence; two units while sitting after the last 'Isha count as one unit; eight units at dawn are the night prayer; the even (Shaf') is two units, the odd (Witr) is one unit, and the two units of Fajr are after the Witr; eight units before Dhuhr and eight units before Asr.

Prayer is recommended at the beginning of the times. The merit of congregational prayer over individual prayer is twenty-four times. Do not pray behind a sinful person, and do not follow except those of Divine Leadership.

Do not pray while wearing the skins of a dead animal, even if tanned seventy times, nor the skins of beasts. Do not prostrate except on the earth or what the earth produces, except for what is edible, cotton, and linen.

In the opening of the prayer, one says: 'Ta'ala Arshak' (Exalted is Your Throne), and it is not said: 'Ta'ala Jaddak' (Exalted is Your Grandeur). And in the first Tashahhud, it is not said: 'As-salamu alayna wa ala ibadillah is-salihin' because the termination of the prayer is the Taslim, and if you say this, your prayer has ended.

Shortening (Qasr) is valid after eight Farsakhs, which is two Barids. If you shorten, you break your fast. Whoever does not shorten on a journey, their prayer is not valid because they have added to what God has prescribed.
Qunut in all prayers is a mandatory Sunnah in the second unit before bowing and after recitation.

Funeral prayer has five Takbirat; whoever reduces them has opposed the Sunnah. The male corpse is lowered feet first, and the female is lowered sideways from the side of the grave. Graves are squared (leveled) and do not rise.
Saying 'Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim' aloud in prayer is obligatory. The pillars of prayer are seven: Time, Purity, Orientation, Qibla, Bowing, Prostration, and Supplication.
Zakat is an obligatory duty on every two hundred Dirhams, which is five Dirhams. It is not obligatory on less than that from silver.
Zakat is not obligatory on wealth until a full year passes from the day the owner acquired it.
Zakat should not be given except to those of Divine Leadership and Recognition.
Zakat is obligatory on gold when it reaches twenty Mithqals, in which case half a Dinar is due.

Zakat is obligatory on wheat, barley, dates, and raisins when they reach five Wasqs. The Zakat is one-tenth if irrigated by rain (natural flow), and one-twentieth if irrigated by wells. One Wasq is sixty Sa's, and one Sa is four Mudds.

Zakat is obligatory on sheep when they reach forty-one, in which case one sheep is due up to one hundred and twenty-one. If one more is added, two are due up to two hundred and one. If one more is added, three are due up to three hundred and one. After that, for every hundred, one sheep is due.

Zakat is obligatory on cows when they reach thirty, a Tabi' (one-year-old) is due. Up to forty, one Tabi'. Then a Musinnah (three-year-old) up to sixty. If sixty, two Tabi's up to seventy. Then one Tabi' and one Musinnah up to eighty. If eighty, two Musinnahs up to ninety. Then three Tabi's. After that, for every thirty cows, one Tabi', and for every forty, one Musinnah.

Zakat is obligatory on camels when they reach five, one sheep is due. If ten, two sheep. If fifteen, three sheep. If twenty, four sheep. If twenty-five, five sheep. If one more, a Bint Makhad (two-year-old female). If thirty-six, a Bint Labun (three-year-old). If forty-six, a Hiqqah (four-year-old). If sixty-one, a Jadh'ah (five-year-old) up to eighty. If one more, a Thani (three-year-old male) up to ninety. If ninety, two Bnat Labun. If one more to one hundred and twenty-one, two Hiqqahs that are ready for breeding.
When camels increase, for every forty, a Bint Labun, and for every fifty, a Hiqqah. The sheep are dropped after that, and it returns to the ages of camels.

Zakat al-Fitr is obligatory on every head, small or large, free or slave, male or female. It is four Mudds of wheat, barley, dates, or raisins, which is a complete Sa. This should not be given except to those of Divine Leadership and Recognition.

key_terms.بِنْتُ مَخَاضٍ: A specific age of camel (two years)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific rulings for obligatory prayers, funeral prayers, and Zakat on livestock and crops in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This excerpt from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal* provides a comprehensive overview of *fiqh al-akbar* (major jurisprudence), detailing the precise structure of the five daily prayers and the specific conditions for their validity, such as the necessity of Qunut and the ruling on shortening prayers during travel. It further elaborates on the ritual of funeral prayers and the intricate calculation of Zakat across various assets, emphasizing the Shia distinction that Zakat is exclusively due to the *Ahl al-Wilayah* (the Imams and their deputies).
